h1: 22 vs 24 Pallet Trailers: Which Semi Suits Your Load?

jsonLd.headline: 22 vs 24 Pallet Trailers: Which Semi Suits Your Load?
jsonLd.description: 22 vs 24 pallet trailers explained: how many pallets fit, when weight matters more than floor space, and how to pick the right semi. Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: How many pallets fit on a semi-trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 24-pallet trailer holds 24 standard Australian pallets in a single layer, and a 22-pallet configuration holds 22. The right number for your load also depends on weight, not just floor space.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a 22 and 24 pallet trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mainly pallet positions and how the trailer is set up for weight. A 24 fits more pallets, which suits light, bulky freight. A 22 can suit heavier freight that hits mass limits before the deck fills.

mainEntity.name: Which trailer is better for heavy freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: For heavy, dense freight, pallet count matters less because you hit the legal weight limit first. A 22-pallet setup is often more practical for heavy loads, since a 24 would just have empty positions to stay legal.

mainEntity.name: Why does weight matter as much as pallet count?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trucks have legal mass limits. Dense pallets can reach that limit before the deck is full, so loading purely by pallet count risks going overweight or leaving freight behind. Always give weight and pallet count together.

mainEntity.name: What should I tell my carrier when booking a trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give the pallet count, the pallet type and the total weight. With those, your carrier can recommend the right trailer to move your freight in one efficient, legal run.

mainEntity.name: What if my load needs more than one trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are higher-capacity options depending on the freight and route. It's worth asking rather than assuming you need two separate runs, since the best option depends on the destination and road access.

mainEntity.name: Does a 24 pallet trailer always carry more than a 22?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only for light freight that fills the deck before hitting the weight limit. For heavy freight you reach the legal mass limit first, so the extra pallet positions can't be used and a 22 setup may suit better.

mainEntity.name: What information decides the right trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: The pallet count, the pallet type and the total weight. Weight is often the deciding factor, so giving both figures lets your carrier pick the trailer that moves your freight legally in one run.

mainEntity.name: Do you need special permits for a full pallet load?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard 22 and 24-pallet loads within mass limits don't need special permits. Oversize or overmass loads are different, and we'll advise if your freight crosses into that territory.

mainEntity.name: Can you mix pallet sizes on one trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within reason. Non-standard pallets change how many fit and how they're restrained, so tell your carrier the pallet types and we'll work out the best layout.

h1: Chain of Responsibility (COR) Explained for Shippers

jsonLd.headline: Chain of Responsibility (COR) Explained for Shippers
jsonLd.description: A plain-English guide to Chain of Responsibility (COR) for businesses that send freight: what it is, who it covers and how to stay compliant. Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: What is Chain of Responsibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chain of Responsibility, or COR, is the law that spreads legal responsibility for heavy-vehicle safety across everyone involved in a freight task, including the operator, consignor, consignee, loader and schedulers, not just the driver.

mainEntity.name: Who does COR apply to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any party with control or influence over a heavy-vehicle transport task. That can include the transport company, the business sending or receiving freight, the loader, packers and schedulers, and managers whose decisions affect safety.

mainEntity.name: What does COR require businesses to do?

acceptedAnswer.text: To take all reasonable steps to ensure the safety of their transport activities, covering vehicle mass and loading, load restraint, speed and driver fatigue. In practice that means safe loading, realistic schedules and using compliant carriers.

mainEntity.name: Can I be responsible under COR if I only send freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. As a consignor you're in the chain. Overloading a truck, poor restraint from your dock, or setting delivery times that pressure a driver to speed or skip breaks can all create COR responsibility.

mainEntity.name: How does using a compliant carrier help?

acceptedAnswer.text: A carrier that restrains to rating, manages driver fatigue and maintains its vehicles handles a large part of the chain for you, which reduces your COR exposure and helps keep your business compliant.

mainEntity.name: Is this legal advice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This is general information only. For advice on your specific obligations, refer to the NHVR's guidance or speak with a suitably qualified adviser.

mainEntity.name: Does COR only apply to the truck driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. COR applies to everyone with control or influence over the freight task, including consignors, consignees, loaders, packers and schedulers, which usually means the businesses at both ends of a delivery.

mainEntity.name: Can I contract out my COR responsibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can't sign away a safety duty you have influence over. You can take reasonable, documented steps to manage it, including using a compliant carrier, but the duty itself stays with you.

mainEntity.name: Where can I read the official COR rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: The NHVR publishes guidance on Chain of Responsibility and the Heavy Vehicle National Law. It's the authoritative source for your obligations, and worth reading alongside advice from a qualified adviser.

mainEntity.name: Does good COR practice also protect my freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Proper loading and restraint keep the truck safe and keep your goods from shifting in transit, so compliance and undamaged deliveries tend to go hand in hand.

h1: FTL vs LTL: Choosing Full Truck Load Freight

jsonLd.headline: FTL vs LTL: Choosing Full Truck Load Freight
jsonLd.description: FTL vs LTL explained: what full truck load and part load freight mean, the pros and cons of each, and how to pick the right one. From Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: What does FTL mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: FTL stands for full truck load. One truck is dedicated to your freight and travels direct from pickup to delivery, with no other customers' goods on board and no depot stops.

mainEntity.name: What does LTL mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: LTL stands for less than truck load, also called part load. Your freight shares a truck with other consignments and usually passes through a depot to be sorted, which is efficient for small loads but slower.

mainEntity.name: Is FTL cheaper than LTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: For small loads, LTL is usually cheaper. Once your freight fills most of a trailer, FTL is normally cheaper per pallet and faster, because you're not paying toward handling other goods. Price large loads both ways.

mainEntity.name: Which is faster, FTL or LTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: FTL is faster. A dedicated truck goes straight to the destination, so transit is essentially the drive itself. LTL waits for a full vehicle and passes through a depot, which adds time.

mainEntity.name: Is FTL better for fragile freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. FTL is loaded once and unloaded once, with no depot sorting in between, so there are far fewer chances for fragile or high-value freight to be damaged.

mainEntity.name: Can one full load be delivered to multiple sites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Because the truck is dedicated to you, an FTL run can include a planned multi-drop to two or three related sites while keeping the direct-transit advantage.

mainEntity.name: At what point does FTL become cheaper than LTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Roughly once your freight fills more than half to two-thirds of a trailer. At that point you're paying part-load rates on a near-full load, and a dedicated truck is often cheaper per pallet as well as faster.

mainEntity.name: Can you help me decide between FTL and LTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Tell us the pallet count, weight, destination and how urgent it is, and we'll advise honestly which method moves your freight best. Sometimes it's FTL, sometimes a part load.

mainEntity.name: Does FTL always mean a full trailer of my own freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the truck is dedicated to your consignment. It doesn't have to be physically full, but you're paying for the whole vehicle, which pays off once your load fills much of the trailer or timing is tight.

mainEntity.name: Can fragile freight go on LTL?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, but every depot handling step adds risk. For fragile or high-value goods, FTL's single-handling, direct run is usually the safer choice, even if the load is small enough that LTL would otherwise be cheaper.

jsonLd.description: What hot shot freight is, when it's worth paying for, and how to get urgent deliveries right. A practical guide from Road Linx Transport in Brisbane.

mainEntity.name: What is hot shot freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hot shot freight is an urgent, dedicated delivery where one truck carries only your load direct from pickup to destination, with no other stops. It's used for time-critical freight that can't wait for a scheduled service.

mainEntity.name: When is a hot shot worth the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: When the cost of waiting is higher than the cost of a dedicated truck. That's usually the case for breakdown parts, freight left off a load, urgent orders or site materials, where downtime or a lost customer costs far more than the run.

mainEntity.name: Is a hot shot faster than normal freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A hot shot goes direct with no consolidation or depot stops, so it's much faster than standard freight that shares a truck and may be sorted at a depot along the way.

mainEntity.name: How should I book urgent freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call rather than email, so the carrier can dispatch immediately. Have the pickup and delivery, a rough idea of the load, and the urgency ready, and flag any access issues so the right truck goes out the first time.

mainEntity.name: Can hot shots run after hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a carrier that keeps the capacity. Urgent freight often lands out of hours, so a carrier who runs early morning, late night and weekend hot shots can solve a problem before it costs you the next day.

mainEntity.name: How do I book a hot shot with Road Linx?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call 07 3179 7072 straight away with the pickup, destination and how urgent it is. Urgent work is best booked by phone so we can dispatch a dedicated truck immediately.

mainEntity.name: How do carriers dispatch hot shots so quickly?

acceptedAnswer.text: By deliberately keeping some trucks and drivers available for urgent work rather than committing every vehicle to scheduled runs. That spare capacity is what lets them dispatch a dedicated truck at short notice.

mainEntity.name: What should I ask a carrier about urgent freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask how they handle urgent and after-hours work and whether they keep capacity for it. A carrier who plans for rush jobs can dispatch quickly, while one running every truck flat out will struggle when you need one.

mainEntity.name: Can a hot shot include a wait and return trip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For urgent jobs we can wait and bring something back, or run a round trip, if that's what the job needs. Tell us the full task up front.

mainEntity.name: Is same-day freight the same as a hot shot?

acceptedAnswer.text: They overlap. Same-day means it's delivered that day; a hot shot is a dedicated, direct run, which is the fastest form of same-day freight for genuinely urgent loads.

mainEntity.name: What should I look for in a Brisbane freight company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check compliance (NHVR and Chain of Responsibility), equipment (load-rated restraint and a range of trucks), coverage across your whole delivery area, and reliability including after-hours and same-day capability. Weigh value, not just price.

mainEntity.name: Why does compliance matter when choosing a carrier?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because a non-compliant carrier risks your freight and, under Chain of Responsibility, potentially your own business's liability. A carrier that restrains to rating and manages fatigue and vehicles protects you as well as themselves.

mainEntity.name: Is the cheapest freight quote the best choice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not usually. A damaged pallet, missed window or failed delivery costs far more than a small saving on the rate. The best value is a carrier that's compliant, well-equipped, reliable and easy to deal with.

mainEntity.name: Why is single-carrier coverage better?

acceptedAnswer.text: A carrier who covers your whole delivery area on their own trucks avoids handovers to other companies, which add time, cost and damage risk. You also get one point of contact and one team accountable.

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask a freight company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask about NHVR and COR compliance, load-rated restraint, their range of trucks, whether they cover your whole area themselves, whether they offer after-hours and same-day work, and how they handle problems.

mainEntity.name: Does Road Linx cover all of Brisbane and beyond?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We cover Brisbane, the Port and metro, plus the Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Toowoomba, the Wide Bay and Northern NSW, all on our own trucks, with after-hours, same-day and relief capability.

mainEntity.name: Is a much cheaper freight quote a red flag?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. A quote well below everyone else usually means something has been cut, whether compliance, insurance or reliability. Look at the whole picture rather than just the number.

mainEntity.name: What are warning signs of a poor carrier?

acceptedAnswer.text: Vagueness about load restraint or NHVR compliance, being hard to reach before you've booked, and quotes that seem too cheap to be sustainable. Good carriers are clear, contactable and upfront.

mainEntity.name: How many freight companies should I compare?

acceptedAnswer.text: Comparing two or three gives you a sense of fair pricing and service without dragging the process out. Judge them on compliance, equipment, coverage and reliability, not just the number.

mainEntity.name: Should I use one carrier or several?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most businesses, one capable carrier covering your whole area is simpler and more reliable than juggling several, since you get one point of contact and one team accountable.

jsonLd.headline: NHVR Compliance & Load Restraint: A Shipper's Guide
jsonLd.description: An introduction to NHVR compliance and load restraint for businesses that send freight: what the rules cover and why load-rated equipment matters. Road Linx.

mainEntity.name: What is the NHVR?

acceptedAnswer.text: The NHVR is the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator, which administers the Heavy Vehicle National Law across most of Australia, setting and enforcing standards for vehicle safety, maintenance, mass limits, driver fatigue and load restraint.

mainEntity.name: What is load restraint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Load restraint is keeping freight secured so it can't move while the truck is travelling. It must hold under the forces of braking, accelerating and cornering, so the load stays put no matter what the truck does.

mainEntity.name: What does load-rated equipment mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Load-rated equipment, such as rated straps, chains and curtains, is engineered and certified to hold a stated load rating. It lets a driver restrain freight to a known standard rather than guessing whether general-purpose straps are strong enough.

mainEntity.name: Why does load restraint matter to me as a shipper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under Chain of Responsibility you share legal responsibility for freight being safe, so poor restraint from your dock can come back to you. Good restraint also means your freight arrives undamaged, since a load that doesn't move doesn't get damaged.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a carrier is compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask whether they run load-rated restraint, whether their drivers are trained in load restraint, and whether they're NHVR compliant and maintain their vehicles. Clear, confident answers are a good sign.

mainEntity.name: Is this compliance advice?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This is general information only. For advice on your specific obligations, refer to the NHVR's guidance or speak with a qualified adviser.

mainEntity.name: What are the main load restraint methods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tie-down, which presses the load onto the deck with straps or chains; blocking or containment, which uses gates, headboards or the trailer structure to stop movement; and direct restraint, which lashes the load to anchor points. They're often combined.

mainEntity.name: Why does load restraint take time to do properly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the freight has to be secured to hold under braking, cornering and acceleration, using the right method and rated equipment for that load. A few minutes of proper restraint prevents shifted or damaged freight and keeps the load legal.

mainEntity.name: Does load restraint really affect whether my freight arrives intact?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A load that's properly restrained doesn't shift in transit, so it's far less likely to be damaged. Good restraint protects your goods as well as road safety.

mainEntity.name: Where can I learn more about load restraint standards?

acceptedAnswer.text: The NHVR publishes load restraint guidance that sets out the principles and methods. It's the authoritative reference, and a good carrier will already work to it.

jsonLd.description: What a tail-lift truck is, how tailgate delivery works, and when you need one for sites with no forklift. A practical guide from Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: What is a tail-lift truck?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tail-lift truck has a powered platform on the back that raises and lowers freight between the deck and the ground, so it can deliver heavy or palletised goods to sites with no forklift or loading dock.

mainEntity.name: What is tailgate delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tailgate delivery is a delivery made using the truck's tail lift to lower the freight to ground level, rather than relying on a forklift or dock at the destination. It suits shopfronts, homes and small sites.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a forklift for a tailgate delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The tail lift does the lifting, operated by the driver, so you don't need a forklift or a loading dock at your end. That's the whole purpose of the service.

mainEntity.name: How much can a tail lift handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the truck, but tail lifts comfortably handle standard pallets and heavy single items within their rating. Tail-lift trucks range from about three to 12 tonnes, so they cover small and large loads.

mainEntity.name: Does a tail lift work on grass or gravel?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, but it works best on firm, level ground. Soft, uneven or sloped surfaces can limit it, so tell your carrier the surface so they can plan the safest approach.

mainEntity.name: Can tail-lift delivery be part of a bigger run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Tail-lift trucks are used within distribution runs, taxi truck jobs and warehouse moves wherever a drop has no forklift. Just flag the sites without lifting gear.

mainEntity.name: Who operates the tail lift, me or the driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: The driver operates the tail lift. They're trained to know the platform's rating, position the load and lower it under control, which keeps the delivery safe for everyone.

mainEntity.name: What can make a tailgate delivery unsafe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mainly soft or sloped ground and an unstable load. That's why the platform needs firm, level footing and the freight is positioned and restrained on it, and why it helps to tell your carrier the site conditions in advance.

mainEntity.name: Is tailgate delivery more expensive than standard delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can carry a small premium for the equipment, but it often saves money overall by avoiding failed deliveries and manual-handling risk at sites with no forklift.

mainEntity.name: Can a tail-lift truck handle multiple pallets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Larger tail-lift trucks handle multiple pallets and heavy items within the platform's rating, all to a ground-level site.

h1: Tautliner vs Curtainsider vs Flat Top: A Trailer Guide

jsonLd.headline: Tautliner vs Curtainsider vs Flat Top: A Trailer Guide
jsonLd.description: A clear guide to trailer types: tautliners, curtainsiders, flat-tops and drop-decks, what each is for and how to pick the right one. Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tautliner and a curtainsider?

acceptedAnswer.text: There's no difference. They're two names for the same trailer, one with tensioned curtain sides that open for side loading and close to protect freight. Tautliner came from a brand name, curtainsider is the generic term.

mainEntity.name: When should I use a flat-top instead of a tautliner?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a flat-top for freight that's oversize, craneable, or too big or heavy for curtains, such as steel, timber and machinery. Use a tautliner for palletised stock that needs weather protection and fast side loading.

mainEntity.name: What is a drop-deck trailer for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A drop-deck has a lower rear deck so it can carry taller loads while staying within the legal height limit, which a standard flat-top couldn't. It's the choice when height is the constraint.

mainEntity.name: Which trailer is best for palletised freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually a tautliner. It loads fast from the side with a forklift and protects the freight from weather, and on load-rated trailers the curtains form part of the restraint.

mainEntity.name: Can building materials go on a tautliner?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, if they fit within the curtains and load from the side. Long, tall or craneable materials are better on a flat-top or drop-deck, which are built for that kind of load.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which trailer I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell your carrier what you're moving, the dimensions, whether it needs weather protection and how it loads. Those answers point to the right trailer. Road Linx can advise and supply the right one.

mainEntity.name: Do different trailers need different load restraint?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On a load-rated tautliner the curtains and internal gear help restrain the load, while a flat-top relies entirely on straps, chains and gates applied to the freight. Open-deck loads take more care to restrain correctly.

mainEntity.name: Which trailer is fastest to load and unload?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually a tautliner, because the curtains open along the whole side for direct forklift access to any pallet, rather than reaching in from the back as with a ute.

mainEntity.name: Are drop-deck tautliners a thing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A drop-deck tautliner combines the lower deck for height with curtain sides for weather protection and fast loading, giving you both advantages in one trailer.

mainEntity.name: Can one carrier supply all these trailer types?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-equipped carrier can. We run tautliners, flat-tops and drop-decks in 22 and 24-pallet sizes, so we match the trailer to your load rather than forcing a fit.

acceptedAnswer.text: A taxi truck is a truck booked for a single job, like a taxi. It moves your load direct and you pay for the trip rather than a day rate. Sizes range from small utes to trucks around 12 tonnes.

mainEntity.name: Is a taxi truck cheaper than hiring a truck for the day?

acceptedAnswer.text: For one-off and ad-hoc loads, yes. You pay for the trip rather than a full day, so you're not paying for hours you don't use. For all-day work, a day hire or standing run may be better value.

mainEntity.name: What can a taxi truck carry?

mainEntity.name: Do taxi trucks run outside business hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Book a tail-lift taxi truck and the driver can lower heavy or palletised items to ground level without a forklift or dock at either end.

jsonLd.headline: What Is B2B Transport & Why It Protects Your Freight
jsonLd.description: What B2B transport is, how business-to-business freight works, and why cutting out depot handling protects your goods. A guide from Road Linx Transport.

mainEntity.name: What does B2B transport mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: B2B transport means business-to-business freight, delivered directly from one business to another. You load at your premises and your customer unloads at theirs, with the freight carried straight through on one truck rather than sorted at a depot.

mainEntity.name: Why does B2B reduce freight damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the freight isn't unloaded, sorted, stored and reloaded at a depot. It's handled once at your end and once at your customer's, so there are far fewer chances for pallets or cartons to be knocked or crushed.

mainEntity.name: Is B2B faster than depot-based freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. B2B freight goes direct rather than waiting at a depot for consolidation and sorting, so transit time is essentially the drive itself.

mainEntity.name: Who loads and unloads B2B freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: You load your goods at your premises and your customer unloads at theirs, each with your own forklift or dock. The carrier restrains and drives the load in between, keeping both businesses in control of their own goods.

mainEntity.name: What if my customer can't unload the freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tail-lift truck can bridge the gap, lowering the freight to ground level without a forklift. So deliveries to smaller business customers can often still run as a direct B2B job.

mainEntity.name: Can B2B be set up as a regular service?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. B2B freight is usually repeat business, so it's often set up as an account with standing runs to your regular customers, capturing how each likes to receive freight.

mainEntity.name: Can B2B transport be set up as an ongoing service?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It's usually set up as an account with standing runs, capturing each customer's delivery windows, access and preferences, so deliveries happen reliably without booking each one.

mainEntity.name: How does B2B make my business look more reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Direct, on-time, undamaged deliveries reflect well on you, since customers judge you partly on how your freight arrives. A well-run B2B setup makes your deliveries something customers can count on.

mainEntity.name: Is B2B only for full pallet loads?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. B2B works for full and part-pallet deliveries alike. The defining feature is direct delivery with no depot handling, not the size of the load.

mainEntity.name: Can B2B go interstate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We run B2B freight down the Brisbane to Northern NSW corridor, keeping the direct, no-depot handling all the way across the border to your customer's dock.

mainEntity.name: What is a time-slot delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: A time-slot delivery lands your freight inside a booked window at the receiver's site, such as a distribution centre dock slot. The truck must arrive within that window, so the run is planned around it to avoid a rejected or rebooked load.

mainEntity.name: Do you deliver after business hours?

mainEntity.name: Why deliver early in the morning?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a delivery misses its DC slot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Missing a distribution centre slot can mean the load is rejected, rebooked days later, or penalised. We plan runs to hit the window and load for a fast unload, so the delivery goes through cleanly.

mainEntity.name: Can you handle overnight warehouse restocks?

mainEntity.name: Is after-hours delivery more expensive?

mainEntity.name: Do you provide proof of on-time delivery?

mainEntity.name: Can time-slot delivery be a regular arrangement?

mainEntity.name: What does B2B transport mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: B2B transport means business-to-business freight, delivered directly from one business to another. You load at your premises and your customer unloads at theirs, with the freight carried straight through on one truck rather than sorted at a depot.

mainEntity.name: Why does B2B reduce freight damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the load isn't unloaded, sorted, stored and reloaded at a depot in the middle. It's handled once at your end and once at your customer's, so there are far fewer chances for pallets or cartons to be knocked or crushed.

mainEntity.name: Is B2B transport cheaper than standard freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's often more efficient because there's no depot handling, and for full or part-pallet business deliveries it can work out very competitively. Pricing depends on your volumes and runs, which we'll quote to your specific supply pattern.

mainEntity.name: Who loads and unloads B2B freight?

acceptedAnswer.text: You load your goods at your premises and your customer unloads at theirs, each with your own forklift or dock. Our driver carries and restrains the load in between. This keeps both businesses in control of their own goods.

mainEntity.name: Can B2B freight be palletised?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, most of it is. We carry palletised B2B freight on load-rated trailers and restrain to rating, so your pallets travel stable and arrive square, which reflects well on your business with your customer.

mainEntity.name: Do you set up regular B2B runs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. B2B freight is usually repeat business, so we set it up as an account with standing runs to your regular customers. You get consistent drivers, predictable timing and less rebooking.

mainEntity.name: Can you deliver B2B within customer delivery windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Where your customer only receives goods in set windows, we build time-slot and after-hours delivery into the B2B run so their receiving rules don't become your problem.

mainEntity.name: Does B2B work for freight from the Port of Brisbane?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We move cleared import stock directly from the Port of Brisbane to your customer's warehouse as a B2B run, avoiding an extra depot stop for freight that's already been handled enough.

mainEntity.name: How do I set up B2B transport?

mainEntity.name: Can my customers book their own deliveries with you?

mainEntity.name: Do you handle returns between businesses?

mainEntity.name: What is a tautliner?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tautliner is a trailer with tensioned curtain sides instead of solid walls. The curtains open for fast forklift loading from either side and close to protect the freight from weather. It's also called a curtainsider.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a tautliner and a curtainsider?

acceptedAnswer.text: They're the same thing. Both names describe a trailer with curtain sides. Tautliner is a common brand-derived term and curtainsider is the generic description, but the trailer is identical in function.

mainEntity.name: Why choose a tautliner over a flatbed?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tautliner loads from the side like a flatbed but also protects freight from the weather and, on load-rated trailers, uses the curtains as part of the restraint. A flatbed suits oversize, craneable or very tall loads that curtains can't enclose.

mainEntity.name: Does tautliner hire come with a driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We supply the tautliner with one of our licensed, load-restraint-trained drivers, so you don't need to source a driver or manage compliance and maintenance yourself.

mainEntity.name: How many pallets does a tautliner hold?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our tautliners come in 22 and 24-pallet configurations. The right one depends on your pallet type and weight, and we'll advise which suits your load.

mainEntity.name: Are the curtains strong enough to restrain the load?

acceptedAnswer.text: On load-rated tautliners the curtains and internal restraint are rated as part of the load-restraint system. Our drivers restrain to that rating, keeping the freight secure and the job compliant.

mainEntity.name: Is freight protected from rain on a tautliner?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once the curtains are closed and tensioned, the freight is shielded from rain, wind and road grime for the journey, which suits cartons, packaging and moisture-sensitive stock.

mainEntity.name: Can I hire a tautliner for one job or ongoing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. We hire tautliners for a single run, for seasonal peaks, or as an ongoing arrangement where the trailer and driver work as part of your operation.

mainEntity.name: How do I arrange tautliner hire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call 07 3179 7072 or email admin@roadlinxtransport.com.au with your pallet count, weight and route. We'll confirm the tautliner size and the hire.

mainEntity.name: Can a tautliner carry building materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, provided they fit within the curtains and load in a way a forklift can handle from the side. Very long, tall or craneable materials are usually better on a flat-top or drop-deck, and we'll advise which suits.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a curtain is damaged?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our trailers are maintained and curtains are checked as part of that. A load-rated tautliner relies on its curtains and internal restraint working together, so we don't run a trailer with compromised curtains on a rated load.

mainEntity.name: Do tautliners use internal gates and load bars?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On a load-rated tautliner the driver uses internal gates, straps and load bars alongside the rated curtains to lock the freight against movement. It's a complete restraint system, not curtains on their own.

mainEntity.name: Can you supply a tautliner and driver for ongoing work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Beyond single runs, we hire tautliners with a driver on an ongoing basis so the trailer effectively becomes part of your fleet without the ownership, maintenance or compliance falling on you.

mainEntity.name: What is a flatbed truck used for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A flatbed, or flat-top, is an open trailer with no sides or roof, used for freight loaded by crane or forklift from the top or sides. It suits steel, timber, machinery and oversize or awkward loads that won't fit an enclosed trailer.

mainEntity.name: What is a drop-deck trailer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A drop-deck is a flatbed with a lower rear deck section. The lower deck lets it carry taller freight while staying within the legal height limit, which a standard flatbed couldn't do with the same load.

mainEntity.name: When should I use a drop-deck instead of a flat-top?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a drop-deck when the load is tall enough to risk breaching the height limit on a standard flat-top. The lower deck keeps a tall load legal without special over-height arrangements.

mainEntity.name: Can you move oversize loads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We handle oversize and awkward freight and can talk you through routing and any permits an over-dimension load needs. Send us the dimensions and weight and we'll confirm what's involved.

mainEntity.name: How is freight secured on an open deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our drivers restrain open-deck loads to the rating on load-rated gear, using the right mix of straps, chains and gates for the freight, under Chain of Responsibility obligations. There are no walls doing the work, so correct restraint is critical.

mainEntity.name: Do flatbeds come with a driver?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Flatbed and drop-deck transport is supplied with one of our licensed, load-restraint-trained drivers who secures the load correctly for the trip.

mainEntity.name: What kinds of freight are not suited to a flatbed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Palletised freight that needs weather protection is usually better on a tautliner. Flatbeds are for heavy, long, oversize or craneable loads where an open deck is an advantage rather than a problem.

mainEntity.name: Can I load a flatbed with a crane on site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The open deck is designed for crane loading from above, as well as forklift access from the sides. Tell us how the load will be lifted and we'll make sure the truck suits.

mainEntity.name: How do I book flatbed or drop-deck transport?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call 07 3179 7072 or email admin@roadlinxtransport.com.au with the load dimensions, weight and how it will be loaded. We'll confirm the right trailer and a price.

mainEntity.name: Do you arrange permits and escorts for oversize loads?

acceptedAnswer.text: We can guide you through what an over-dimension load needs, including permits and pilot or escort requirements, and handle the transport. Give us the exact size and weight so we can confirm what applies.

mainEntity.name: What's the height limit before I need a drop-deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard trucks have a legal height limit, and a tall load can breach it on a flat-top. A drop-deck lowers the deck to buy height. Send us the load height and we'll tell you which trailer keeps it legal.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a flat tray and a flatbed?

acceptedAnswer.text: They describe the same open-deck idea. Flat tray, flat-top and flatbed all mean a trailer or truck with an open deck and no sides or roof, loaded by crane or forklift. We run them from small flat-tops up to semi-trailer decks.

mainEntity.name: Can you carry steel and long lengths safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Steel, timber and long lengths are common flatbed freight. Our drivers restrain them to rating with the right chains, straps and gates, so long or heavy loads stay secure for the whole trip.

mainEntity.name: How much downtime does a warehouse move need?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a sequenced plan and an after-hours or weekend run, many businesses reopen at the new site with only hours of lost trading rather than days. The exact figure depends on the size of the move and the access at both ends, which we work through when we plan it.

mainEntity.name: Do you move pallet racking as well as stock?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We move dismantled racking, shelving, stock, fit-out and machinery. We coordinate with your team or your installer on dismantling and reinstalling the racking so the transport side lines up with it.

mainEntity.name: Can you relocate a warehouse over a weekend?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it's often the smart choice. Moving overnight or across a weekend means the business is closed during the disruption and reopens already stocked at the new address.

mainEntity.name: What if the new site has no forklift or loading dock?

acceptedAnswer.text: We bring tail-lift trucks so heavy and palletised items can be lowered to ground level safely without a forklift or dock. That's a common situation with new or interim premises and we plan for it.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle machinery and plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Plant and machinery are loaded and restrained to the rating on load-rated equipment. For very heavy or oversize machinery we'll confirm the right trailer, usually a flat-top or drop-deck.

mainEntity.name: How many trucks will my move need?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on the pallet count, racking and machinery involved. We size the fleet during planning so the move runs in as few trips as practical without leaving trucks waiting around on your clock.

mainEntity.name: Do you cover moves outside Brisbane?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We relocate warehouses and factories across South East Queensland and into Northern NSW, including moves between regions such as Brisbane to the Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast or Toowoomba.

mainEntity.name: Is my stock insured during the move?

acceptedAnswer.text: We move freight under Chain of Responsibility with load-rated restraint, and we'll confirm the cover that applies to your relocation when we quote. For high-value stock, tell us up front so we can advise on the right arrangement.

mainEntity.name: How far ahead should I book a relocation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The earlier the better, because planning is where the savings are. For larger moves, a few weeks' notice lets us sequence it and lock in an after-hours window. We can still help with shorter timeframes when needed.

mainEntity.name: Do you supply the crew to load and unload?

acceptedAnswer.text: We supply drivers and can arrange loading crew for the move. For specialist racking or machinery dismantling we'll coordinate with your installer or fitter so the transport lines up with it.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to be on site during the move?

acceptedAnswer.text: It helps to have someone from your team at both ends to direct where things go, especially for a sequenced move. We'll agree the plan beforehand so everyone knows the running order.
